newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan markets seen mixed ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan markets seen mixed ahead of expiry.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to be mixed this week, moving in a limited range as market players may be wary of taking large new positions ahead of the spot expiry on September 24, traders said on Tuesday.

"Uncertainty over the spot expiry continues to cast a shadow over the markets. Overall expectations of a large number of deliveries at the expiry will make local investors cautious of any fresh buying," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The benchmark February contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 138.6 yen per kg, down from 140.6 yen last Friday.
The benchmark February contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was 138.9 yen per kg in the second morning session, down from 140.0 yen last Friday.
Traders said the spot expiry next Tuesday hinges on how market bulls and market bears manoeuvre the markets and the power balance between the two.
Market bulls, led by one trade house, usually take delivery while market bears try to deliver massive amounts of rubber at the expiry in an attempt to push down prices.
Traders said any upside potential in Japanese markets would likely be limited as fundamental and technical factors indicate bearishness, despite some bullish factors in overseas markets.

"Fundamentally, continued rises in Japan's rubber stocks will make buyers cautious, while massive speculative long positions in the September contract at TOCOM, could put a lid on the any price rally," said a Tokyo-based technical analyst at a commodity broker.
Traders said, however, that any price falls would also be limited as the Thai government is likely to support the physical market.
One trader also said rising rubber stocks in Japan have been mostly discounted in TOCOM's spot price, while he suggested the spot contract on Kobe has more room to fall on easing near-term supplies.
Thai rubber offer prices to Japan were steady to firmer, quoted at 128 U.S. cents as of Tuesday, up one cent from last Friday.
In the local physical market, Thai benchmark rubber to large-lot end-users was quoted at 146 yen per kg as of Tuesday, up from 144 yen on September 10.
